questions.question: How do radio buttons form a group where selecting one unselects the others?
options: By sharing the same name attribute
By sharing the same id attribute
By being wrapped in the same <div>
By sharing the same value attribute
questions.hint: The name attribute ties radio buttons into an exclusive group.
questions.explanation: Radio buttons must share the exact same 'name' attribute value to belong to the same mutually exclusive selection group.

questions.question: Which input type provides built-in browser email address format validation?
questions.explanation: type="email" enforces email syntax validation and displays an optimized keyboard on mobile devices.

questions.question: Which attribute ensures an input field must be filled in before form submission?
questions.explanation: The required boolean attribute stops form submission if the input field is blank.

questions.question: Which attribute accepts a Regular Expression (Regex) to validate custom input formats?
questions.explanation: The pattern attribute takes a JavaScript regular expression that the input's value must match.

questions.question: Why is client-side HTML validation alone insufficient for web security?
options: It can be disabled or bypassed by inspecting the DOM or using API tools
It only works on desktop browsers
questions.explanation: Client-side validation can be disabled in developer tools or bypassed via automated HTTP requests; server-side validation is always required.
